notes: The host sends APNs itself when it holds the key (thread L6). Live, the hub could not reach Apple: a Worker's fetch speaks HTTP/1.1 to origins and APNs refuses it (every push ended as 'APNs network error'). New src/main/server/remote/apns.ts: ApnsSender over node http2 with token auth (the ES256 provider token kept 50 minutes and re-minted on a 403, one session per gateway reused across pushes, a 5xx, timeout or network error tried three times, 410, BadDeviceToken, Unregistered and DeviceTokenNotForTopic answered as gone) from TEMP_CODE_APNS_KEY_PATH, _KEY_ID and _TEAM_ID (TEMP_CODE_APNS_URL points at an h2c test server); apnsPayload.ts carries the hub's alert and liveactivity payload builders so both sides post one shape. PushRegistry with a sender relays every registration locally, takes its devices back from the hub at boot, posts each notifier notice to the phones that asked for its event (a gone token drops the row, another failure lands on it) and pushes Live Activity states to the thread's tokens; the ActivityFeed delivers locally when told to. index.ts wires the sender from the environment and closes it on shutdown. scripts/ios-device.sh gains TC_DEVICE_METHOD=ad-hoc (a Release archive exported with automatic distribution signing and installed), the build whose production token the owner's Production-only APNs keys need. Tests: apns.test.ts (6, an in-process h2c APNs with the JWT verified against the generated public key), push.test.ts (+3). CLAUDE.md, infra/hub/README.md and docs/box.md say so.
